examples.name: Default
examples.summary: A standard data-driven table: pass `:data` and `:columns` and the engine renders sortable headers, status `Tag`s, per-row action menus, and pagination. The outer card border is drawn via the `border` prop — the table is borderless by default (it usually sits inside a surface that already frames it), so set `border` to draw the `var(--border-default)` outline; the internal row dividers are unaffected either way.

examples.name: Composition
examples.summary: The compound API: build the table by hand from `<Table.Header>` / `<Table.Row>` / `<Table.HeadCell>` / `<Table.Cell>`. The result is an ordinary table — the same as the data-driven API — but you control every cell. Reach for it when a cell needs custom content; otherwise prefer `:data` + `:columns`.

examples.name: WithCheckboxes
examples.summary: A leading selection column (`enable-row-selection`): each row gets a checkbox and the header gets a select-all box that reflects the all/none/indeterminate state. Selection is exposed via `v-model:row-selection`; changes log to the Actions panel.

examples.name: CompactHeader
examples.summary: A denser header via `header-kind="compact"` (forwarded to `Table.Header`): the column-header row uses a reduced height and padding, so the table opens straight onto that header row.

examples.name: SelectedRow
examples.summary: A row in the selected state: the second row is pre-selected via `v-model:row-selection`, rendering the `var(--bg-selected)` surface and `aria-selected`. With `select-on-row-click`, clicking anywhere on an inert part of a row toggles its selection.

examples.name: FixedLayoutWithColumnSizes
examples.summary: Every column declares an explicit pixel `width`, so the layout is fixed: columns keep their declared size instead of distributing to fill the surface, and the viewport scrolls horizontally if the widths sum past it.

examples.name: ColumnWidthFloors
examples.summary: The two short-content columns declare a **`minWidth`** floor instead of a fixed `width`. The table measures each of them — its header (sort affordance included) and every rendered cell — and pins the column to whichever is larger, as one width shared by the header and every body cell. **Status** settles on its header, because the chips under it are shorter than the word; **Protocol** grows past the floor to fit `HTTP & HTTPS`. A fixed `width` is a bet in both directions: wide enough for the protocol wastes space on the status, tight enough for the status truncates the protocol. The measured width tracks the rendered page, so paging or sorting longer content into view can widen the column.

examples.name: ResizableColumns
examples.summary: A simple table whose columns opt into drag-to-resize via per-column `resizable: true`. Drag a header divider: only that column resizes (the others freeze at their current width) and the table grows with horizontal scroll. A column can shrink only down to its own content width. Frozen and action columns ignore `resizable`.

examples.name: StickyColumn
examples.summary: Extra columns (Protocol, Domains, Origins, Created) push the rows past the surface. The **Name** column is pinned to the start edge (`frozen: "start"`) and the **actions** menu to the end edge (`frozen: "end"`): both stay put while the middle columns scroll horizontally underneath, with a CSS-only edge fade dissolving the scrolling content under each pinned column.

examples.name: CompactHeaderWithStickyColumn
examples.summary: A compact header (`header-kind="compact"`) combined with the freeze system: the frozen **Name** / **actions** columns stay pinned while the middle columns scroll horizontally, and the denser header is sticky within the scroll viewport. No pagination.

examples.name: Empty
examples.summary: When `data` is empty, the table renders a default empty state in the `#empty` slot — an illustration, a title, and a short description. Override the `#empty` slot to supply your own copy and call-to-action (e.g. a Create button or a documentation link).

examples.name: VirtualRows
examples.summary: Ten thousand rows with `virtual`: only the rows in view render (plus a few above and below), the rest are space, so the table mounts and scrolls fast. The viewport scrolls within `max-height` (40rem when empty); `estimate-row-height` is the starting guess until a row is measured.

examples.name: WithCollection
examples.summary: Server mode of `useCollection`: `fetch` receives the text, sort, page and page size (and an abort signal) and returns one page and the total; `tableProps` binds data, loading, sorting, pagination and selection in one `v-bind`, and selection survives paging.

examples.name: CellPresets
examples.summary: The cell presets every list shares: `Table.CellLink` for a name that opens another screen (tooltip names the destination) and for a domain with its `+N` overflow and a copy button pinned to the end edge, `Table.CellId` with a copy button, `Table.CellStatus` (one semantic chip per row), `Table.CellTags` showing as many tags as fit, `Table.CellTime` (avatar plus relative time, the absolute time on the tooltip and for screen readers) and `Table.CellActions` (the row menu named after the row).

examples.name: ReorderableRows
examples.summary: `reorderable` adds a leading grip to every row: drag it, or focus it and press Arrow Up, Arrow Down, Home or End. The table emits `update:data` with the new order (bind `v-model:data`) and `reorder` with `{ from, to, row }`, announces each move in a polite status region, and locks the grips while a sort is applied.

examples.name: ReorderableFrozen
examples.summary: A reorderable table with a frozen first column and row selection: the grip and the selection checkbox stay pinned at the start edge, side by side, while the other columns scroll under them.

examples.name: Refresh
examples.summary: The refresh pattern: `Table.RefreshButton` with `loading` spins while the current rows stay on screen, an `Updated` line beside it uses `Table.CellTime` (relative, absolute on the tooltip, re-rendered every minute), and auto-refresh is off by default, runs every 30 seconds when turned on and skips a tick while the tab is hidden.

examples.name: TreeRows
examples.summary: Hierarchical rows: `get-sub-rows` returns each row's children, which open under a chevron in the principal column, indented one step per level. The grid becomes a `treegrid` (`aria-level`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-posinset`) with one row in the tab order: Arrow Up and Arrow Down move between rows, Arrow Right opens a row or enters it, Arrow Left closes it or goes to the parent, Enter toggles it and Space selects it. `v-model:expanded` holds the open rows; selection stays per row.

examples.name: StackedRows
examples.summary: A short release list in a side-panel-width box with `stackable`: each row becomes a card with the release name as its title and Area and Released as label and value lines. Opt-in; a console list keeps its scrolling grid on a phone.
